title: New Hires and a New Role on Audience

body_markdown:
Jennie Coughlin is now National’s senior audience editor, and Nathan Boley and Kerrie Vila join The Times.


As the Audience team continues to grow, we’re excited to announce a new role for one of our sharpest editors and two new members of the team. Please join us in congratulating Jennie Coughlin on her new role as National’s senior audience editor and in welcoming Nathan Boley and Kerrie Vila to The Times.


Credit: Earl Wilson


After an exceptional four years as Metro’s desk audience editor, Jennie Coughlin has stepped into the role of senior audience editor on National.


Since joining The Times in 2019, Jennie has proven herself to be among the Audience team’s sharpest, most knowledgeable and collaborative editors, leading training sessions across the newsroom and being on top of the day’s latest trends before some of us are awake.


Editors on Metro described Jennie as the desk’s “secret weapon,” where she helped The Times find audiences for big stories like historic city elections and Trump on trial, while using data to identify new opportunities for key desk franchises such as Metropolitan Diary.


I can think of no better audience editor to help us find new readers for coverage of the country, a view shared by her colleagues on National. “Jennie is a true audience maestro, and a real partner to the editing team on National,” said Nestor Ramos. “She has the ability to dive into complex reams of audience data and emerge with sharp, actionable insights. If the answer exists, she knows how to find it. She makes our report better every single day.”


In addition to her work on National, Jennie will continue to serve as a leader on the growing Desk Audience Editors team and the Audience team as a whole, as well as a partner to me as we continue to refine how we collaborate across the newsroom to help our report be as sharp and well-read as it can be every day.


Jennie joined The Times in 2019 as a member of the Search team. Previously, she worked in local newsrooms in New Jersey, upstate New York, Virginia and Massachusetts.


— Jake Grovum


Credit: Earl Wilson


---


Nathan Boley has joined Audience as our new audience editor for Washington.


In this role, which is based in the bureau, Nathan will partner closely with editors and reporters to help identify the desk’s biggest opportunities for coverage. Supporting strategy across the report, he will share insights on performance and identify new opportunities to engage Times readers, including in new formats like video and community features.


As a member of the Desk Audience Editors team, he will be a partner to the desk on live and breaking news coverage, helping shape plans before major news moments and offering real-time guidance as stories develop.


“We are delighted to welcome Nathan to Washington and look forward to his insights and contributions to the team,” said Charo Henríquez, Washington’s strategy and operations deputy.


Before joining The Times, Nathan was the director of audience at the Houston Chronicle, where he led the newsroom’s audience team and developed strategies to grow readership across search, social, newsletters, the app and the home page.


Previously, Nathan held audience roles at news organizations in California, Pennsylvania and his home state of Ohio. He graduated from Ohio University with degrees in English and history and is a lifelong (and long-suffering) Pittsburgh Pirates fan.


— Jenna Fowler


---


Kerrie Vila is our new audience editor for Graphics, Weather and The Upshot.


Kerrie has already hit the ground running, partnering with Graphics and The Upshot on major projects including election results and polling. She will play a key role in shaping audience strategy for the remainder of the midterm cycle.


She will also work with the Weather desk on everything from their forecast coverage strategy to breaking storm and weather-related news.


Kerrie will be working closely with our Data & Insights team to help translate audience data into editorial strategies for her desks and the broader Desk Audience Editors team.


Before joining The Times, Kerrie served as director of content analytics for Hearst Newspapers, where she oversaw centralized strategy for analytics reporting and planning across the organization’s eight local markets. She previously worked at News Revenue Hub, consulting with local nonprofit newsrooms on audience and membership growth strategies.


“I’m especially excited to learn from Kerrie’s experience working on weather strategy for local news outlets and to incorporate her insights into our coverage and plans,” said John Keefe, Weather Editor.


Kerrie is moving back to New York for her new role. She is looking forward to being close to her family and friends and dreading her first Northeast winter in almost a decade.


— Jenna Fowler
